children: heads into its September 30 fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report with its stock already up roughly 266% this year, but Stifel analyst Brian Chin still sees substantial upside. Chin expects another earnings beat and argues that investors are underestimating how long tight DRAM supply, rising contract prices and booming AI-memory demand could support Micron's earnings and margins.
We believe the durability of this memory upcycle continues to be under-appreciated, Chin opined.
The supply-demand imbalance is central to his thesis.

Chin's industry checks suggest DRAM bit shipment growth could slow to roughly 15%-20% in calendar 2027 from the mid-to-high 20% range expected during 2026. Yet he believes demand would require DRAM bit supply growth would need to be 40-50%+ in CY27 to really bridge the supply deficit.
That gap could keep memory pricing unusually strong.

Chin forecasts Micron's gross margin reaching 87% in the September quarter and rising further to 88.2% in the November quarter. HBM4 could add another layer of upside, with the analyst expecting HBM4 price/bit will likely double as next-generation AI accelerators require more premium memory.

For fiscal Q4, Chin projects $50.78 billion of revenue and adjusted earnings of $32 per share. His November-quarter forecast rises to $56.4 billion, or roughly 11% sequential growth, driven primarily by pricing rather than higher shipment volumes.

Micron's earnings report is increasingly about the durability of the memory shortage rather than simply beating quarterly estimates. Investors should watch DRAM contract pricing, HBM4 negotiations, gross-margin guidance and management's plans for new capacity beginning around mid-2027. Chin maintains a Buy rating and $1,500 price target, implying about 44% upside from Monday's close. If Micron confirms that supply remains constrained into 2027 while HBM pricing strengthens, the current upcycle could have considerably further to run.

title: Stifel Has Message For Micron Stock Investors Before Earnings
